structured_output.summary: Attempt 3 fixes all four findings from attempt 2. A newly added source now goes through a full compare against an empty document, so webhooks, root and info x- keys and unknown component sections fail closed. type_changed and constraint_changed at schema-subtree positions now scan the new side. operation_removed binds the whole removed operation. Added securitySchemes are checked against a known key set. CLASSIFIER_VERSION is 3 and the ledger matches it. The recorded checks for source beeec1f… all pass with exit 0: airs_drift --check, 45 drift tests (up from 42), --require-through-phase 25, and an unchanged SDK diff. Some gaps remain, all low: replacing a parameter, body or response $ref with inline content is reported as type_changed without a scan, and existing security schemes and operation servers are not checked against a key set. No blocker, high or medium findings. Total 44.5/50.

findings.description: compare_reference reports a $ref replaced by inline content (or the reverse) on a parameter, request body or response as type_changed at a pointer that ends in a name, 'requestBody' or a status code. Those pointers are not in SCHEMA_SUBTREES (120-121), so the emit hook at 435-438 never scans the new inline side. A discriminator, not or x-* inside it is reported as breaking instead of failing closed. Attempt 2 named this '$ref→inline' case and it is only partly resolved. The same hole applies when compare_schema turns a non-dict schema into a dict at a property-name pointer (696-697).
findings.required_fix: In compare_reference, when the new side is an inline dict, call scan_parameter, scan_body or scan_response (whichever matches the caller) before emitting. In compare_schema's non-dict branch, call scan_schema on a dict new side. Add a test where a response $ref is replaced by inline content whose schema contains discriminator.

findings.description: compare_security_scheme reports any new key on an existing scheme, including x-* extensions, as security_scheme_changed. Added schemes, by contrast, fail closed on keys outside SECURITY_SCHEME_KNOWN (532-535), so the two paths are inconsistent.
findings.required_fix: Fail when an added or changed key on an existing scheme is not in SECURITY_SCHEME_KNOWN. Add a test that adds x-rotation to an existing scheme.

findings.description: scan_operation does not check the operation's effective servers or security entries against a known key set, so server variables or x- keys on a newly added operation pass as additive.
findings.required_fix: Scan the servers entries of an added operation (allowing url, description and variables) and fail on unknown keys. Add one test.

evidence: The checks file (attempt-03.checks.json) has source_sha256 beeec1f… and passed=true. I grepped it for non-zero exit codes and timeouts and found none.
checks.json:2302-2321: `airs_drift.py --check` exit 0, 'pinned baseline verified; ledger current; baseline self-compare unchanged'.

checks.json:2322-2352: test_airs_drift ran 45 tests OK (42 in attempt 2), including test_added_source_structures_outside_operations_and_components_fail_closed, test_new_subtrees_reported_as_type_or_constraint_changes_are_scanned and test_operation_removed_identity_binds_the_whole_operation.
checks.json:2403: --require-through-phase 25 printed 'upstream drift baseline verified; drift reported, never adopted'.
checks.json:2272-2280: `git diff --exit-code b66133892b… -- crates/scm-sdk Cargo.* LICENSE NOTICE` passed, so the SDK was not mutated.

airs_drift.py:988-993: an added source is compared in full against an empty same-version document, which resolves attempt-2 medium #1. Tests at test_airs_drift.py:443-460 cover webhooks, root x-, info x-, a components.callbacks section and a securityScheme x- key, plus a clean source_added case.

airs_drift.py:435-438 with SCHEMA_SUBTREES (120-121): a type_changed or constraint_changed new side at anyOf, oneOf, allOf, prefixItems, items, additionalProperties, propertyNames or schema is now scanned, which resolves most of attempt-2 medium #2. Tests at test_airs_drift.py:462-473.
airs_drift.py:808: operation_removed now uses old=old[key], which resolves attempt-2 low #1. Test at test_airs_drift.py:475-481.
airs_drift.py:532-535 and 122: added securitySchemes are checked against SECURITY_SCHEME_KNOWN, which resolves attempt-2 low #2.
airs_drift.py:37 sets CLASSIFIER_VERSION = 3, and contracts/airs-drift.json:245 records classifierVersion 3. The ledger regeneration check passed.
The plan (docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:254-303) matches the implemented behavior: offline check and compare, refresh as the only networked path, and drift reported but never adopted.
limitations: Read-only review. I did not run any tests or tools myself; all execution evidence comes from the recorded checks file.
I sampled the 3278-line checks file and grepped the rest for failures and timeouts rather than reading every entry.

I did not re-audit check_phase.py, test_management_phases.py, red_team_management.py or the vendor 0.86.0 bytes beyond the recorded passing checks. Earlier attempts accepted them, and this attempt's changes are concentrated in airs_drift.py and its tests.
I found the remaining gaps (inline $ref replacement, existing security-scheme keys, operation servers) by reading the code and did not reproduce them with a run.
I did not examine remote CI or a live pan.dev refresh.
